10.1002_cssc.71166: Decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) offers a unique strategy for green hydrogen production by separating the hydrogen and oxygen evolution reactions either in time or space, with the potential for integration to intermittent renewable energy sources. This review highlights the critical assessment of DWE, including the different components used and the operational strategies to accelerate the hydrogen economy. Special emphasis is placed on redox mediator engineering, catalyst innovation, membranes, and next-generation cell architectures to overcome current limitations associated with conventional electrolyzers including efficiency, stability, and cost. The in silico approaches, including density functional theory and molecular dynamics-driven parameter optimization can accelerate DWE by bridging the gap between lab-scale technology development and industrial scale-up, thereby facilitating the rise of DWE as one of the next-generation technologies for green hydrogen production. A visionary roadmap is proposed, showing the pathway from proof-of-concept laboratory studies toward market deployment, with the aim of recognizing DWE as a cornerstone technology for a sustainable, low-carbon hydrogen future. The review is conceptualized based on literature survey and identified research gaps.
10.1016_j.ejrh.2026.104189: Study region The Sangabeol underpass in Gwacheon, South Korea, receives road network runoff at a single low point, examined using a local rainfall record and two additional records from Taean and Naju. Study focus A process-based module couples runoff, routing, effective drainage, and storage-depth conversion with 5-min warning updates, using an effective drainage parameter (η = 0.85) fitted to one approximate depth–time observation and absorbing multiple uncertainties. Rolling forecasts and full-record reference simulations separate accumulation dynamics from rainfall-coverage and warning-rule effects; a hydraulic diagnostic estimates approach-flow depth and velocity from simulated discharge. New hydrological insights for the region Early shallow accumulation alone did not determine subsequent depth-rise rates. Simulated 10–15 cm and 15–20 cm transitions had 60-min/31-min (Gwacheon), 14-min/13-min (Taean), and 23-min/11-min (Naju) durations. The Taean–Naju ranking reversal links evolving rainfall and routed inflow to changing accumulation rates, so an initially slower rise need not imply more time at higher depths. Approach-flow velocities (0.33–0.89 m/s) reversed similarly between the two intervals, indicating discharge contrasts originating upstream of the low point. Predicted remaining times at first Danger were 26–27 min, reflecting the 30-min decision window and 5-min update cycle; limited future rainfall caused 21-, 2-, and 2-min delays in first-Alert 20-cm crossings relative to the full-record reference. These results support interpreting depth, velocity, crossing-time updates, and rainfall coverage for this configuration and retrospective inputs.
10.1021_acs.est.5c12882: Microplastics (MPs), due to their poor degradability, can accumulate in the body following ingestion. Most studies evaluating MP safety use pristine particles or those aged for a short period, thus overlooking the long-term physicochemical changes that MPs undergo once they are trapped in tissues. In this study, we observed pronounced alterations in the surface properties of polystyrene MPs after one year of exposure to artificial body fluids, including increased surface roughness and hydrophilicity. These changes enhanced the adhesion of biomolecules, such as lipopolysaccharide (LPS), a typical pathogen-associated molecular pattern (PAMP). Biomechanical analysis confirmed strong interactions between aged MPs and LPS. Once phagocytosed by macrophages, LPS-loaded aged MPs caused phagolysosomal damage and pyroptosis through noncanonical caspase-11 inflammasome activation, which in turn amplified canonical caspase-1-dependent inflammation. Importantly, the inflammatory impact of aged MPs was further validated in vivo in a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis model in which aged MPs aggravated disease severity. Collectively, these results identify aged MPs as “Trojan horses” with enhanced ability to transport harmful extracellular biomolecules like LPS into the cytoplasm, thereby reprogramming inflammasome signaling. This study highlights particulate stimuli, such as aged MPs, as a previously unrecognized bridge-linking PAMPs with danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs).
